policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'shall indeed bring me again' renders an emphatic doubled verb of the root shuv in the hiphil sense 'bring back'. The qere yashov (infinitive absolute) and the ketiv yashiv (hiphil imperfect) both yield the same English 'indeed bring me again'; nothing in the wording names one form over the other. The only notes are a gloss on Aram and an alternative_rendering on 'serve', neither of which touches this unit. Base fallback retained.

ASV 'should I this day make thee go up and down with us' is the causative sense of the root nua shared by both spellings; qere ani'akha and ketiv anu'akha differ only in orthography of the same hiphil form and produce identical English. No note is mapped to this verse. Base fallback retained.

ASV text reads 'at the fords of the wilderness', which is the ketiv be'avrot ('fords', root avar). The textual_variant note 'Another reading is, in the plains' is the qere be'arvot (arabah/plains), which the ASV relegated to the margin. The wording therefore distinguishes the ketiv.
